## Scope and status {#sec-fs-scope}

This chapter builds the gene panel on which the covariances of
@sec-cov-scope are estimated. It is the application that the
feature-selection vignette
([3.1](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html))
leaves to this book: filters as applied, settings, rank tables and
code. It runs on the single-cell counts of GSE229513 at the three
bulk-matched times (@sec-geo-design), one time at a time. What the
panel must achieve, and why each step is there, is stated in the
vignette
([3.1, what the genes are for](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#wrn-fs-estimand)):
genes whose type-level moments can be estimated in every type and that
carry information about $\boldsymbol{p}$. The sections follow the tiers
of the vignette: (i) quality control and prior knowledge, (ii)
cross-cell consistency and (iii) cross-platform consistency are
implemented here; (iv), down-weighting by the model, is a remark: it
takes place when DeCovarT itself is fitted (@sec-fs-weighting-pointer).

The Suppinger reference is the one-specimen case of that callout. It is
one technical scRNA-seq experiment
[@suppingerMultimodalCharacterizationMurine2023], and its cells are
draws from one specimen, not biological replicates (@sec-geo-design).
Every ranking statistic below is therefore computed inside that
specimen: it calibrates a screen, not a population-level claim of
differential expression. 

::: {#nte-pseudoreplication .callout-note}
## :information_source: Cells are not biological replicates

Treating the cells of one specimen as independent replicates of a
population contrast is pseudoreplication: it inflates the apparent
sample size and understates the standard error of every statistic
computed across cells
[@zimmermanPracticalSolutionPseudoreplication2021;
@squairConfrontingFalseDiscoveries2021;
@crowellMuscatDetectsSubpopulationspecific2020]. A score fitted this
way, or a bootstrap that resamples cells with labels fixed, measures
generalisation to new cells of this specimen, not to new specimens. It
is reported as such wherever it is used in this book
(@sec-cov-scope, @sec-sens-scdesign3).
:::

The current panel (top 500 per time, @sec-fs-export) comes from the
legacy between/within ratio
([between/within ratio](#sec-fs-ms-ratio)). Once tiers (i) to (iii)
have been run, their rank replaces it as steps 3 to 5 of
@fig-pipeline, and every output of @sec-cov-scope has to be refitted.

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Tier (i): quality control and prior knowledge {#sec-fs-qc}

The vignette lists the quality-control rules of the reviewed methods
as examples
([3.1, QC](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-qc)).
Here the authors' quality control is taken as given, and those rules
are recorded against it rather than applied again. This tier also
holds what is decided without the counts: the curated markers, forced
into the panel, and the presence gate.

### Cell and gene QC as applied {#sec-fs-qc-applied}

The deposited object is the authors' filtered matrix: 27,027 genes and
71,005 cells, with the same cells in the raw counts and in the `SCT`
layer (@sec-seurat). `scripts/02_01_stats_quality_control.R` has been
run on it. Its outputs in `output/feature_selection/tier_01/` are three
summary tables (`cell_counts.csv`, `author_qc_audit.csv`,
`gene_filter_summary.csv`) and `scored_slots.rds`, which holds every
per-gene and per-cell table and is tracked with DVC
(`dvc pull output/feature_selection/tier_01/scored_slots.rds.dvc`).
The figures are drawn by `scripts/02_01_vis_quality_control.R`.
@tbl-fs-qc-compare sets the authors' choices, the deposited counts,
the examples of the vignette and this book side by side.

| Item | Suppinger et al. | Deposited counts (scored cells) | Examples in the vignette | This book |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Detected genes per cell | kept if > 1,800 | minimum 1,548; 65 of 20,437 cells at ≤ 1,800 | deMixSC: removed if < 200 | no new filter |
| Mitochondrial counts | kept if < 10 % | not computable: no `mt-` gene deposited | deMixSC: removed if > 50 % | no new filter |
| Library size | not reported | minimum 1,443; no cell below 500; 417 cells beyond 3 MAD of their type | deMixSC: removed if < 500; RNA-Sieve: 3 MAD from the type median (optional) | recorded, not applied |
| Doublets, ambient RNA | not reported | — | — | none |
| Mitochondrial, ribosomal, Gm genes | removed after the cell QC | no `mt-`, `Rpl` or `Rps` symbol | BayesPrism: ribosomal and mitochondrial genes removed | already absent |
| Sex-chromosome genes | kept | present (*Xist*, *Ddx3y*, *Kdm5d*, *Uty*) | BayesPrism: removed | kept |
| Low-detection genes | none on the raw counts (3,599 genes are zero in every cell); `SCTransform` models genes detected in ≥ 5 cells of a batch | 19,275 genes detected in ≥ 5 cells of both batches | RNA-Sieve: ≥ 20 % of the cells of one type; deMixSC: ≥ 5 % of all cells | presence gate: ≥ 5 % of the cells of every scored type, variance > 0 |
| Variable genes | 3,000 integration features, 2,944 left in `SCT` | — | — | recorded, not a filter |
| Multi-mapping UMIs | Salmon/Alevin 1.1.0 splits them | 12.8 % of non-zero entries fractional | — | genes > 90 % fractional dropped |

: Quality control of the Suppinger reference: the authors' choices (STAR Methods, "Quality control and filtering", and the settings stored in the object), what the deposited counts show on the 20,437 scored cells of the three slots (`author_qc_audit.csv`; element `gene_rules` of `scored_slots.rds`), the examples of the [review table of 3.1](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#tbl-fs-review), and what this book applies. {#tbl-fs-qc-compare}

**Cells.**

- **The authors' thresholds stand.** They kept cells with more than
  1,800 detected genes and less than 10 % mitochondrial counts
  [@suppingerMultimodalCharacterizationMurine2023]. Both cut-offs are
  stricter than the deMixSC examples (200 genes, 50 %), so no fixed
  rule of the vignette removes a cell they kept. They were computed
  before the mitochondrial, ribosomal and Gm genes were removed: the
  mitochondrial fraction needs the chrM genes. That order is an
  inference, not a statement of the paper. It explains why 65 scored
  cells fall at or below 1,800 genes on the deposited genes, and why
  the mitochondrial fraction cannot be recomputed:
  `cell_mitochondrial_fraction()` returns `NA`, not 0, when no `mt-`
  symbol is present.
- **Library-size outliers are recorded, not removed.** 417 scored cells
  (239 at 48 h, 69 at 72 h, 109 at 96 h) lie beyond 3 scaled MADs of
  the log library size of their type (`cell_qc_rules()`). They pass
  the authors' QC, which is taken as given.
- **Slot filter.** `keep_bulk_matched_cells()` keeps cells with a time
  slot in {48 h, 72 h, 96 h}, a non-missing `celltypeannotation` and a
  library size above zero. The library size is the column sum of the
  deposited counts over all 27,027 genes; it equals $10^{\texttt{log\_umi}}$
  of the authors' `SCTransform` models, whereas the metadata column
  `nCount_RNA` does not, and is not used.
- **Artefacts and small types.** The culture-stress labels flagged
  `include_in_ranking = FALSE` in
  `data/dictionaries/suppinger_celltype_crosswalk.csv` (Cd63+
  ectoderm-like artefact, Zscan4+ artefact) are dropped. A type with
  fewer than `min_cells = 20` cells in a slot is left out of the
  scores; exiting naïve pluripotency at 72 h (8 cells) is the only such
  case.

(a) Detected genes against library size, both on log scales, one point per cell coloured by cell type; dashed lines mark the Suppinger cut-off (1,800 detected genes) and the deMixSC cut-offs (200 genes, 500 counts); circled cells lie beyond 3 scaled MADs of the log library size of their type. (b) Distribution of the log10 library size per type, types ranked by median, with the median (point), the ±3 MAD interval (bar) and the number of cells in the label. @fig-fs-low-quality shows the authors' cells against the cut-offs. Every
cell sits far above the deMixSC lines. The cells below the 1,800-gene
line are the low tail of a single library-size–gene trend, not a
separate population, and the 3-MAD flags fall at both ends of that
trend.

**Genes.**

- **Bulk symbols.** Every one of the 27,027 symbols appears in the bulk
  HTSeq `gene_name` column; `shared_bulk_single_cell_genes()` drops the
  49 whose rows carry more than one Ensembl id once the version suffix
  is removed (element `shared` of `scored_slots.rds`). `drop_mitochondrial_genes()` is kept
  as a guard and removes nothing here.
- **Fractional counts.** The deposited counts are Salmon/Alevin
  estimates. A UMI compatible with several genes is divided among them,
  equally when no read tells them apart, so 12.8 % of the non-zero
  entries are fractions such as 1/2, 1/3 or 1/4. The share is not tied
  to expression level; it concentrates in multi-copy loci (the
  protocadherin-γ cluster, processed pseudogenes, histone genes), whose
  counts are shares of the same UMIs as their paralogues. Their
  within-type correlations are then fixed by the split, not measured,
  which matters for the covariances of @sec-cov-scope. The 2,178 genes
  whose non-zero entries are more than 90 % fractional are dropped
  (495 of them detected in at least 500 cells), the share being
  computed on all 71,005 cells without labels
  (`fractional_count_share()`; elements `fractional` and `dropped_fractional` of `scored_slots.rds`). The
  counts are not rounded: rounding would turn every 0.5 into 0.
  `glmGamPoi` accepts non-integer counts, and the negative-binomial
  likelihood is then a quasi-likelihood.
- **Presence gate.** After these filters 24,816 genes enter the
  presence gate of @sec-fs-presence at each time; 8,643 (48 h), 8,636
  (72 h) and 8,788 (96 h) pass it (element `presence` of `scored_slots.rds`).
- **Authors' gene list.** The 2,944 genes of the `SCT` layer are the
  CCA integration features: 3,000 anchor features, of which 56 (histone
  genes, MHC `H2-` genes, *Nme2*, *4930537H20Rik*) are absent from the
  layer (element `anchor_missing` of `scored_slots.rds`). They are variable
  over all twelve time points and both batches, not a quality filter.
  Of them, 1,622 (48 h), 1,589 (72 h) and 1,562 (96 h) also pass the
  filters above, which pass 7,021, 7,047 and 7,226 genes outside the
  list. The list was the gene set of the legacy panel only
  ([legacy panel](#sec-fs-legacy)).

### Knowledge-driven markers {#sec-fs-markers}

Curated markers are hard prior knowledge: they are united with the
ranked panel at each time whatever their score, so they are chosen
without the counts and cannot be a product of the rank. The list is
short: `data/dictionaries/mouse_gastruloid_signaling_markers.csv`, with
columns `cell_type_excel` (lineage on the signalling map),
`cell_type_suppinger` (the matching Suppinger label, or `NA`) and
`gene_marker`. Symbols are mapped offline with `org.Mm.eg.db`
(`R/02_01_stats_quality_control.R`), not `biomaRt`. The lineage groups of the
same file are the gene modules of the tier (iii) filter
(@sec-fs-bulk-filter).

Fifteen of the 19 mouse symbols are in the 2,944-gene allow-list.
Under a uniform draw of 19 genes from the 27,027 RNA symbols the
expected overlap is about 2.1; the hypergeometric upper tail is
$P(X\ge 15)=8.8\times10^{-12}$ (`marker_sct_hypergeometric.csv`). The
four absent markers are *Myod1*, *Pax6*, *Sox1* and *Tfap2a*
(`venn_markers_vs_counts.pdf`).

### Presence gate {#sec-fs-presence}

A gene enters the ranking at a given time only if it is detected, and
varies, in **every** scored type at that time. With $\delta_{gj}$ the
fraction of cells of type $j$ with a non-zero count for gene $g$, and
$v_{gj}$ the within-type variance of the counts,

$$
\min_{j}\delta_{gj}\ge\delta_{\min}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\min_{j}v_{gj}>0 .
$$ {#eq-fs-presence}

`presence_gate()` in `R/02_01_stats_quality_control.R` returns one row per
gene with `min_detection`, `min_variance` and a logical `pass` that
applies both conditions; $\delta_{\min}$ is the argument `min_frac`,
fixed at 0.05 before the ranks are seen (the default and the value of
every call below). The reasons
for a gate in every type, rather than in at least one, are in
[3.1, presence](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-presence).
In the current outputs the gate is absent. Its absence is one cause of
the constant-gene fallback of the covariance estimates
(@sec-cov-scope).

**Projections of the gated genes.** @fig-fs-pca-plsda projects the
scored cells of each slot on the genes that pass the gate. They are
descriptive, not a selection rule.

- **Input.** The analytic Pearson residuals of the null model $M_0$ of
  @eq-fs-glm (intercept and library-size offset, gene-wise
  negative-binomial overdispersion, `pearson_residuals_m0()`), the
  variance-stabilised scale of the tier (ii) count model, without
  `SCTransform` and without clipping. Genes are centred, not scaled:
  the residuals are already on a common scale, and scaling would
  up-weight genes that carry mostly noise. PLS-DA
  (`mixOmics::plsda()`, two components, cell type as response) uses the
  same matrix. The shifted logarithm $\log(1+x/s_c)$, centred and
  scaled, remains available (`input = "shifted_log"`).
- **Small first axes.** The first two principal components explain
  together 1.3 % (72 h) to 3.1 % (48 h) of the variance: the type
  structure is spread over many genes.
- **Cell line at 48 h.** The epiblast, the large type at 48 h, splits
  into two clouds, and the panels coloured by cell line show that the
  split is the cell line. The sign of the first principal component
  puts 5,301 of the 5,470 B-S (batch 1) epiblast cells on one side and
  5,081 of the 5,120 SBR (batch 2) cells on the other
  (`projection_pc1_by_batch.csv`). Even the PLS-DA, fitted to separate
  the types, separates the two lines on its second component. Cell
  line is therefore the main source of variation within that type,
  which is why the labels of tier (ii) are permuted within batch
  (@sec-fs-omnibus).

The PLS-DA components put the rare types (naïve and ectopic
pluripotency, gut) at the ends of the axes.

## Tier (ii): cross-cell consistency {#sec-fs-consistency}

A gene is kept when its counts separate the scored types consistently
across the cells of one slot. The theory, and the comparison of the
four tests, are in
[3.1, cross-cell consistency](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-consistency).

### Count-model fit per time {#sec-fs-glm}

At each of 48 h, 72 h and 96 h, on the genes that pass the presence
gate and the cells of the scored types, two negative-binomial GLMs are
fitted gene by gene with `glmGamPoi::glm_gp()` [@glmGamPoi2020]:

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_0:\quad \log m_{gc} &= \beta_{0g}+\log s_{c},\\
M_1:\quad \log m_{gc} &= \beta_{0g}+\beta_{g,j(c)}+\log s_{c},
\end{aligned}
\qquad
x_{gc}\sim\mathrm{NB}(m_{gc},\psi_{g}),\quad
\operatorname{Var}x_{gc}=m_{gc}+m_{gc}^{2}/\psi_{g},
$$ {#eq-fs-glm}

with $s_c$ the size factor of cell $c$ (full RNA library size, the
column sum of the deposited counts, divided by its median), passed as
`offset = log(s_c)` with `size_factors = 1` so that it is not applied
twice. `glmGamPoi` reports the overdispersion $1/\psi_g$. For the
likelihood-ratio statistic $\psi_g$ is the gene-wise maximum-likelihood
estimate under $M_1$ and $M_0$ is refitted at the same $\psi_g$; for
the quasi-likelihood test it is shrunk across genes
(@sec-fs-omnibus). Cell type and nothing else is a covariate; cell line
is not (@sec-geo-design).

The ranking statistic is the cell-weighted deviance explained,

$$
R^{2}_{D,g}=1-\frac{\mathcal{D}_g(M_1)}{\mathcal{D}_g(M_0)},
\qquad
\Lambda_g=\mathcal{D}_g(M_0)-\mathcal{D}_g(M_1),
$$ {#eq-fs-deviance-r2}

with both deviances summed over every cell at the same $\psi_g$, so
that $\Lambda_g$ is the likelihood-ratio statistic of the type effect.
Each cell has weight one, which is the weighting of the likelihood
itself; the type-equal weighting of the legacy rank
(@eq-fs-equal-type) is not carried over.

**Why `SCTransform` is not needed.** `SCTransform` fits the same $M_0$
[@hafemeisterNormalizationVarianceStabilization2019;
@choudharyComparisonEvaluationStatistical2022], but with two
departures that matter for a screen of the type effect:

- its overdispersion is regularised across genes, as a smooth function
  of the mean, so a gene whose spread departs from the trend (for
  example a marker that is bimodal across types) gets the wrong
  residual scale;
- its Pearson residuals are clipped at $\pm\sqrt{n/30}$, $n$ the cells
  of the fit (@tbl-fs-sct-settings). Under $M_0$, which has no type
  term, the cells of a rare type that expresses a marker, and the cells
  of a highly expressed gene, have the largest residuals: they carry
  the type signal. Clipping shrinks exactly these high-leverage cells.

Here $\psi_g$ is estimated gene by gene and nothing is clipped. The
`SCTransform` Pearson residual $r^{P}_{gc}=(x_{gc}-\hat m_{gc})/\sqrt{V(\hat m_{gc})}$
is also not standardised. The standardised residual divides it by
$\sqrt{\hat\varphi(1-h_{gc})}$, with $\hat\varphi$ the dispersion
scale (1 for the NB likelihood) and $h_{gc}$ the leverage of cell $c$
(@sec-fs-outliers). The vignette states the model and the residuals
([3.1, count null model and Pearson residuals](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-sctransform)).

### Four tests of the type effect {#sec-fs-omnibus}

`compare_type_effect_tests()` (`R/02_02_stats_cross_cell.R`) computes four
tests of the joint type effect ($J-1$ degrees of freedom) per gene, on
the fits of @eq-fs-glm. They answer one question with different
reference laws; the vignette compares their assumptions
([3.1, four tests](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-omnibus)).

| Column prefix | Statistic | Reference law | Implementation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lr` | $\Lambda_g$, analysis of deviance (@eq-fs-deviance-r2) | $\chi^{2}_{J-1}$ | own deviances from the `glm_gp()` fits |
| `anova_vst` | one-way ANOVA $F$ on $\log(x_{gc}/s_c+y_0)$, $y_0=1/(4\alpha)$, $\alpha=0.05$ | $F_{J-1,\,C-J}$ | matrix sums by type |
| `ql_f` | quasi-likelihood $F$ [@lundDetectingDifferentialExpression2012] | $F$ with empirical-Bayes denominator df | `glmGamPoi::test_de(fit, reduced_design = ~1)` |
| `welch_perm` | Welch's $G$ on the Pearson residuals of $M_0$ | label permutation | Freedman–Lane, $B$ shared permutations |

: The four tests of the type effect as implemented. $C$ is the number of cells of the slot. {#tbl-fs-type-tests}

[TODO-cite: Ahlmann-Eltze & Huber (2023), shifted logarithm]{.highlight}
[TODO-cite: Winkler et al. (2014), Permutation inference for the general linear model, NeuroImage; Freedman-Lane recommended, G statistic Eqs 6-7]{.highlight}
[TODO-cite: Welch (1951), On the comparison of several mean values]{.highlight}

The permutation follows Freedman and Lane
[@freedmanNonstochasticInterpretation1983]: the reduced model is $M_0$,
whose fitted part carries no type information, so permuting its
residuals against fixed labels is the same as permuting the labels.
Welch's $G$ is used because it stays pivotal when the within-type
variances differ, as recommended by Winkler et al. (2014). One
permutation of the $C$ labels is drawn and applied to every gene, $B$
times, and $p_g=(1+\#\{G^{*}_g\ge G_g\})/(B+1)$. $B$ is fixed before
the run (the code default is 2,000). Its floor $1/(B+1)\approx5\times10^{-4}$
limits both the resolution of a gate on this test and Kendall's $\tau$,
since genes at the floor are tied
([3.1, calibration](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-calibration)).

**Permutations within batch.** At 48 h the slot pools the two cell
lines, which are the two batches of the object (B-S in batch 1, SBR in
batch 2), and the type mix differs between them. An unrestricted
permutation would then read a cell-line shift as a type effect.
Labels are therefore permuted within batch (`strata = batch`), which
keeps the type counts of each batch; at 72 h and 96 h each slot holds
one batch, so the restriction changes nothing there. Cell line is
still not a covariate of $M_0$ or $M_1$.

**Gate and rank.** One test is chosen before the ranks are seen and
used as a Benjamini–Hochberg gate over the genes that pass the presence
gate. The gate is the permuted Welch $G$ (`gate_test = "welch_perm"`,
the default of `rank_genes_omnibus()`): in the simulation of the
vignette it is the only test that keeps the false discovery rate at
its nominal level when the within-type variances differ (0.05, against
0.16 to 0.21 for the other tests compared there), at the cost of power
(0.41, against
0.76 to 0.85)
([3.1, four tests](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-omnibus)).
Every gene that passes the gate enters the panel; no cap is imposed
(`n_select = Inf`). The cap of 500 genes per time was inherited from the
legacy panel and had no data-driven justification. The genes that pass
are still ranked by $R^{2}_{D,g}$ (@eq-fs-deviance-r2), ties broken by
$\Lambda_g$, to order and report them. Why a gate followed by an effect
size, rather than a rank by $p$-value, is in the vignette (link above).

The gate controls false discoveries, not relevance. With thousands of
cells, a type effect of any size passes Benjamini–Hochberg, so the panel
contains genes whose effect is real but small. No effect-size floor is
added: their weight is left to the model, through the covariances that
DeCovarT estimates and inverts (tier (iv), @sec-fs-weighting-pointer).

**Multiplicity.** A permutation $p$-value is marginal: one per gene.
The gate is applied to every gene that passes the presence gate, so a
correction across genes is still needed, and Benjamini–Hochberg at
0.05 is applied to the permutation $p$-values of each slot. A false
discovery rate suits a screen whose output is then ranked by an effect
size; a family-wise rate (for example a max-$T$ adjustment from the
same permutations) would discard genes that the rank needs. Three
consequences of the permutation scale are reported with the outputs
(`permutation_floor.csv`):

- with $m$ genes tested, all the genes at the floor $1/(B+1)$ pass
  only when there are at least $m/\{0.05\,(B+1)\}$ of them, about
  $m/100$ for $B=2{,}000$;
- near the Benjamini–Hochberg cut, the Monte Carlo standard error of a
  $p$-value is $\sqrt{p(1-p)/B}$, so a gene close to the cut can move
  across it with another seed;
- each slot is gated at 0.05 on its own. The union over the three
  slots, which feeds tier (iii), has no single false discovery rate;
  a Benjamini–Hochberg over the pooled (gene, slot) $p$-values would
  give one.

```{r}
#| label: fs-omnibus-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. sc[[tm]]: raw counts (genes x cells) of the scored cells of
# slot tm; cell_type[[tm]]: their labels; batch[[tm]]: their batch;
# lib[[tm]]: full library sizes (column sums of the deposited counts).
# B, the seeds and the thresholds are fixed before the run.
source("R/02_00_utils.R")
source("R/02_01_stats_quality_control.R")
source("R/02_02_stats_cross_cell.R")
times <- c("48h", "72h", "96h")
sf <- lapply(lib, function(l) l / stats::median(l))

tests <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  compare_type_effect_tests(
    sc[[tm]],
    cell_type[[tm]],
    size_factors = sf[[tm]],
    n_perm = 2000L,
    seed = 20261101L,
    strata = batch[[tm]],
    fdr = 0.05,
    min_frac = 0.05
  )
})
names(tests) <- times

# Agreement of the gene orders: all tested genes, then those passing
# the gate (permuted Welch G).
tau_all <- lapply(tests, type_test_kendall)
tau_gated <- lapply(tests, function(r) type_test_kendall(r, genes = r$welch_perm_pass))

# Conservativeness: rerun on one within-batch permutation of the labels
# (null by construction) and compare the share of p-values below 0.01
# and 0.05.
calibration <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  null_labels <- withr::with_seed(20261102L, {
    lab <- cell_type[[tm]]
    for (idx in split(seq_along(lab), batch[[tm]])) {
      lab[idx] <- lab[idx][sample.int(length(idx))]
    }
    lab
  })
  res_null <- compare_type_effect_tests(
    sc[[tm]],
    null_labels,
    size_factors = sf[[tm]],
    n_perm = 2000L,
    seed = 20261103L,
    strata = batch[[tm]]
  )
  type_test_calibration(res_null)
})

# Gate on the permuted Welch G, rank by the deviance R^2; the fits and
# permutations of `tests` are reused, not redrawn.
ranked <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  rank_genes_omnibus(
    fdr = 0.05,
    n_select = Inf,
    gate_test = "welch_perm",
    results = tests[[tm]]
  )
})
names(ranked) <- times
# Panel passed to tier (iii): genes selected at any time (the tier (i)
# markers are united with it before export).
panel <- unique(unlist(lapply(ranked, function(r) r$gene[r$selected])))
```

**Results.** `scripts/02_02_stats_cross_cell_consistency.R` has been
run (21 min, 23 GB peak memory). Its outputs in
`output/feature_selection/tier_02/` are `calibration.csv`,
`permutation_floor.csv`, `kendall_<time>.csv`, `selected_<time>.csv`
and `cross_cell.rds` (every test table, tracked with DVC); the figures
are drawn by `scripts/02_02_vis_cross_cell.R`.

- **Calibration.** Under one within-batch permutation of the labels
  (@fig-fs-null-calibration), the analytic tests are anti-conservative
  at 48 h: at the 0.01 level the likelihood ratio rejects 2.9 times the
  nominal rate, the quasi-likelihood $F$ 2.8 times and the
  shifted-log ANOVA 3.4 times. A within-batch permutation keeps the
  association between type and cell line, and these tests do not
  model the cell line, so its effect reads as a type effect. The
  permuted Welch $G$ rejects 0.63 times the nominal rate there. At
  72 h and 96 h, one batch each, every test is at or below its
  nominal rate except the ANOVA (1.2 to 1.4 times at 0.01).
- **Gate.** The permuted Welch $G$ passes 1,417 (48 h), 3,420 (72 h)
  and 5,821 (96 h) of the 8,643, 8,636 and 8,788 tested genes at BH
  0.05. The genes at the floor $1/(B+1)$ (635, 1,686 and 2,869) far
  exceed the about 87 needed for all of them to pass
  (`permutation_floor.csv`), so the floor does not limit the gate.
- **Agreement.** Kendall's $\tau$ between the likelihood ratio and the
  quasi-likelihood $F$ is 0.98 at every time; between the permuted
  Welch $G$ and the other three it is 0.68 to 0.80
  (@fig-fs-test-agreement).
- **Panel.** Every gated gene enters the panel (@fig-fs-gate-rank):
  1,417, 3,420 and 5,821 genes at 48, 72 and 96 h, 6,604 across the
  three times (`selected_<time>.csv`, ordered by $R^{2}_{D}$). The
  largest $R^{2}_{D}$ is 0.60 (*Slc2a3* at 96 h), but 99 % (48 h),
  96 % (72 h) and 89 % (96 h) of the gated genes explain less than 5 %
  of the deviance (median $R^{2}_{D}$ 0.003, 0.005 and 0.010): real but
  small effects, whose weight is the relevance question left to the
  model (tier (iv)).
- **Overdispersion.** The gene-wise $1/\psi_g$ decreases with the mean
  (@fig-fs-overdispersion); a group of genes sits near zero, the
  Poisson limit of the fit.

| Is the nominal tail of each test accurate? | label permutation, one permutation applied to all genes | labels within batch, within the slot |

Cell types are the authors' annotations, fixed before any statistic is
computed here. Labels refined on the same counts would make every
permutation $p$-value anti-conservative
[@gonzalezDelgadoPostclusteringInference2025].

**Conclusion of tier (ii).** [Decision: the panel has no cap and no
effect-size floor. The earlier rule kept the 500 genes with the largest
$R^{2}_{D}$ per time; it came from the legacy panel and had no
data-driven basis, so it is removed, and no threshold on $R^{2}_{D}$
replaces it. The panel is every gene that passes the calibrated gate
(permuted Welch $G$, BH at 0.05): 1,417, 3,420 and 5,821 genes at 48,
72 and 96 h, 6,604 across the three times. The gate controls false
discoveries, not relevance: with thousands of cells per slot, 99 %
(48 h), 96 % (72 h) and 89 % (96 h) of the gated genes explain less
than 5 % of the deviance. Weighting these small effects is left to the
model (tier (iv), @sec-fs-weighting-pointer). Open question: if the
fit of tier (iv) cannot absorb them, an effect-size floor chosen from
the data (for example from the null distribution of $R^{2}_{D}$ under
within-batch permutations) is the next step.]{.highlight}

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Tier (iii): cross-platform consistency {#sec-fs-bulk-consistency}

This tier compares the bulk with the single-cell reference, so it needs
a matched bulk (@fig-suppinger-design). It removes genes whose bulk
expression the reference cannot produce. The approaches reviewed, the
model behind the statistic and its identifiability are in
[3.1, cross-platform consistency](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-cross-platform);
the comparison table of second-generation methods is in
[3.1, review table](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-review-table).

### Outlier cells and genes {#sec-fs-outliers}

Two fits are diagnosed with Cook's distance, which combines leverage
and residual
([3.1, leverage and influence](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-leverage)).

- **Cells**, in the $M_1$ fit of each gene (@eq-fs-glm).
  `cook_cells()` uses the IRLS weight $w_{gc}=m_{gc}^{2}/V(m_{gc})$; in
  a one-way design the leverage is
  $h_{gc}=w_{gc}/\sum_{c'\in j(c)}w_{gc'}$, so a cell of the 29-cell
  somite differentiation front has a leverage near $1/29$ and an
  epiblast cell near $1/10{,}590$. Cook's distance is
  $r^{P\,2}_{gc}h_{gc}/\{J(1-h_{gc})^{2}\}$ with dispersion scale 1.
- **Genes**, in the weighted regression of each bulk replicate on the
  reference signature, across genes. `cook_genes()` takes the
  composition and the final weights of the plug-in fit
  (@sec-fs-bulk-filter) and computes the hat values on the types with a
  positive coefficient.

A cell or a gene is **flagged only when its leverage and its
standardised residual are both large** (defaults: leverage above three
times its mean, $J/C$ for cells and $J/G$ for genes, and
$|r^{SP}|>3$). High leverage alone marks a rare type or a highly
expressed marker, which carries information; a large residual alone
marks an ordinary tail count. Nothing is clipped or down-weighted:
flagged cells and genes are listed with their type and counts, and
whether to drop one is decided by reading that list.

```{r}
#| label: fs-outliers-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. After fs-omnibus-call and fs-bulk-consistency-call: panel
# genes, reference counts, labels, size factors and the tier (iii) plug-in.
source("R/02_03_stats_influence.R")
outlier_cells <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  cook_cells(sc[[tm]][panel, ], cell_type[[tm]], size_factors = sf[[tm]])
})
outlier_genes <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  r <- tail_res[[tm]]
  cook_genes(
    bulk[[tm]][rownames(r$moments$mu), , drop = FALSE],
    r$moments$mu,
    coef = matrix(r$plugin$composition$coef, nrow = ncol(r$moments$mu)),
    weights = r$plugin$weights
  )
})
```

### Bulk consistency filter {#sec-fs-bulk-filter}

The filter needs a single-cell slot and a bulk sample of the same
condition.

- **Matched pairs.** The single-cell reference matches the standard-Wnt
  bulk at all three times used in this book: single-cell 48 h (B-S and
  SBR pooled), 72 h (SBR) and 96 h (B-S), each against three biological
  replicates of the standard-Wnt bulk at that time.
- **No match for early Wnt.** The early-Wnt bulk (Wnt pulse at 24 h)
  has no single-cell counterpart at any time, so no bulk–reference
  comparison is possible on that arm.
- **Fit.** At each of the three matched times independently, in two
  steps. First, a $\boldsymbol{p}$-free check: the distance of each
  normalised bulk value to the range of the type means, with
  RNA-Sieve's range bound and median-absolute-deviation outlier rule
  [@erdmann-phamLikelihoodbasedDeconvolutionBulk2021]
  (`bulk_consistency_filter()`, a heuristic). Second, the tail
  statements below, on a statistic that uses a plug-in composition.
- **Apply (planned, not applied).** The rule was to remove a gene
  flagged at any of the three matched times from the panel at every
  time, including the early-Wnt arm. The run below shows that the
  model-based statements flag 93 to 95 % of the panel under A3, and
  still 70 to 72 % after a cross-fitted gene-wise platform ratio, so
  the rule is not applied (see **Results**).
- **Drift across times.** With three matched times the flags can be
  compared across 48 h, 72 h and 96 h. `platform_drift_summary()`
  classifies each gene by the times at which it is flagged (T4 by
  default) and by the sign of its standardised discrepancy
  $D_{gi}/\operatorname{sd}D_{gi}$: flagged at several times with one
  sign supports treating the platform effect as a property of the
  gene; flagged at one time only does not.
- **Code.** Tier (iii) has two files: `R/02_03_stats_influence.R` (Cook's
  distance for cells and genes, @sec-fs-outliers) and
  `R/02_03_stats_tail_bounds.R` (range check, plug-in, tail statements,
  quantile band, drift, transcript length and the gene-wise platform
  ratio). `scripts/02_03_stats_cross_platform_consistency.R` runs both.
  It has been run; its outputs in `output/feature_selection/tier_03/`
  are `tail_order_<time>.csv` (A3), `platform_drift.csv` (flagged genes
  only), `platform_log_ratio.csv`, `platform_length.csv`,
  `platform_ratio.csv` (cross-fitted $\log_2\hat b_g$ and its standard
  error, per held-out time and method), `a3_shift_summary.csv` (one row
  per time and variant), `settings.csv` and `cross_platform.rds` (every
  table, tracked with DVC). The figures are
  drawn by `scripts/02_03_vis_cross_platform.R`.

**Plug-in composition: deMixSC, not plain NNLS.** For each bulk
replicate $i$, `plugin_composition_demixsc()` fits the bulk counts
$y_{gi}$ on the per-cell type means of the reference by iterated
weighted non-negative least squares, as deMixSC does: weights
$1/(\hat y_{gi}^{2}+(y_{gi}-\hat y_{gi})^{2}+c)$ with $c=2$. Plain NNLS
is not used as a plug-in, for two reasons.

- **Weights of the model.** Under DeCovarT the variance of a bulk count
  is gene-specific and depends on $\boldsymbol{p}$ and on the type
  means. Unweighted NNLS gives every gene the same weight, so the most
  expressed genes decide $\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}$. The deMixSC weights
  are inverse-variance weights that follow the current fit: the
  diagonal, plug-in counterpart of the generalised least squares that
  DeCovarT solves (@sec-deconv-models). Of the two, it is the closer
  to the final model.
- **Robustness to the genes under test.** The residual term
  $(y_{gi}-\hat y_{gi})^{2}$ down-weights the genes that the bulk
  expresses far from the reference, which are the genes this filter
  must find, so that they do not bias $\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}$ and, in
  turn, their own statistic.

Non-negative least squares remains only the solver of each reweighting
step (`nnls::nnls()`, the Lawson–Hanson algorithm). deMixSC also
calibrates a gene set G2 on a same-aliquot benchmark; none exists for
Suppinger, so G2 is empty. $a_i$ is the sum of the coefficients and
$\hat p_{ji}$ the coefficients divided by $a_i$; the extra
overdispersion between platforms is fixed at 1. MuSiC
[@wangBulkTissueCell2019] is not used, because its weights need at
least two donors. What the plug-in costs is in
[3.1, plug-in](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-plugin).

[TODO-cite: deMixSC (Eq. 4, PDF p. 12), iterated W-NNLS weights]{.highlight}
[TODO-cite: Lawson & Hanson (1974), Solving Least Squares Problems, ch. 23]{.highlight}

**Statistic.** With $\hat{\tilde\mu}_{gj}$ the mean raw count per cell
of type $j$ over its $C_j$ reference cells, and $\hat\psi_{gj}$ the
negative-binomial size matched to their mean and variance
(`type_moments_nb()`; raw counts, because a bulk is a sum of raw cell
profiles),

$$
D_{gi}=\frac{y_{gi}}{a_i}-\sum_{j=1}^{J}\hat p_{ji}\,\hat{\tilde\mu}_{gj},
\qquad
S_{Mi}=\sum_{g\in M}\frac{D_{gi}}{\operatorname{sd}D_{gi}},
$$ {#eq-fs-bulk-stat}

for a gene $g$ and a module $M$; $\operatorname{sd}D_{gi}$ is the
negative-binomial standard deviation with $n_i=a_i$ bulk cells.

**Statements.** Each is applied at $\alpha/2=0.01$ per tail, with the
plug-in values treated as known
([3.1, five bounds](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-five-bounds)).
`tail_threshold()` returns the threshold $t_{0.01}$ of each, from the
exact cumulant generating functions and their Legendre transforms for
the Chernoff statements.

| Statement | `method` | Gene | Module | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1, Gaussian (Lindeberg–Feller) | `clt` | yes | yes, independent genes | approximation |
| T1-log, log-normal ratio (delta method) | `clt_log` | yes | no | approximation |
| T2, dependency-graph CLT | `clt_dep` | no | yes | approximation |
| T3, Chernoff with Poisson CGFs | `poisson` | yes | yes, independent genes | bound for Poisson counts only |
| T4, Chernoff with the NB CGF | `nb` | yes | yes, independent genes | finite-sample bound |
| T5, NB Chernoff after a proper colouring | `nb_dep` | no | yes | finite-sample bound |
| Quantile band, `quantreg::rq()` at $\tau=0.01, 0.99$ | — | yes | no | model-free reference |

: Tail statements of the bulk filter as implemented in `R/02_03_stats_tail_bounds.R`. `tail_threshold()` dispatches one function per statement. {#tbl-fs-tail-statements}

[TODO-cite: Janson (2004), Large deviations for sums of partly dependent random variables]{.highlight}
[TODO-cite: Chen & Shao (2004), Normal approximation under local dependence]{.highlight}
[TODO-cite: Koenker & Bassett (1978), Regression quantiles]{.highlight}

- **Modules.** The lineage groups (`cell_type_excel`) of the signalling
  dictionary of @sec-fs-markers. They were written before any count was
  seen, so the module flags are not circular. Each group has at most
  four genes, and a module with fewer than two panel genes is skipped.
- **Dependency graph.** Inside a module, `module_dependency_graph()`
  joins the gene pairs with the largest within-type correlations, with
  maximum degree $\le10$ and mean degree $\le3$. With at most four genes
  both caps are met by construction. Genes without an edge are assumed
  independent; T2 uses the within-type correlations on the edges, T5
  only the colouring of the graph (`greedy_colouring()`).
- **Quantile band.** `quantile_band_flags()` regresses $y_{gi}/a_i$ on
  $\sum_j\hat p_{ji}\hat{\tilde\mu}_{gj}$ across the genes of one
  replicate, at $\tau=0.01$ and $0.99$, without a count model. Each
  bound above bounds a quantile of $D_{gi}$ under a model; the band
  estimates it from the genes, assuming they are exchangeable given
  the fitted value
  ([3.1, comparison of the bounds](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-bounds-compare)).
- **Ranking on the simulated tails.** The vignette compares the
  statements on one gene and one module, which is not a Suppinger
  result
  ([3.1, thresholds](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#tbl-fs-thresholds);
  [gene tails](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#fig-fs-bounds-gene);
  [module tails](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#fig-fs-bounds-module)).
  Per gene, T4 has the largest threshold and does not under-cover.
  Per module, T5 has the largest threshold and does not under-cover.
  T3 is far too small for a high-expression gene.
- **Multiplicity, two counts.** The level 0.01 per tail is per gene.
  In the vignette, that level flags about 60 consistent genes out of
  about 3,000: that count is the vignette's one comparison. Here, the
  Suppinger panel is 6,615 genes times three replicates, which would
  give about 200 (gene, replicate) flags per tail and statement if the
  model held. The run flags about 6,200 genes (below).

**Results.** The panel is the 6,604 genes that pass the tier (ii)
gate at any time, united with the mapped markers: 6,616 genes, of which
6,615 are in each slot. All three variants below run on that panel.

- **What the tail statements assume.** Every statement T1 to T5 tests
  $D_{gi}$ against its spread under assumption A3: each gene has the
  same mean count per cell in the bulk as in the reference, so the bulk
  differs from $a_i\sum_j\hat p_{ji}\hat{\tilde\mu}_{gj}$ only by the
  negative-binomial sampling of $a_i$ cells. With $a_i\approx1{,}200$
  to $1{,}900$ cells that sampling averages out, so
  $\operatorname{sd}D_{gi}$ is small, and a gene is flagged when $D_{gi}$
  is more than about 2.3 of these standard deviations from 0 (T1; the
  Chernoff statements are somewhat wider).
- **What the data show under A3.** The median $|D_{gi}|/\operatorname{sd}D_{gi}$
  is 17 at every time: the discrepancies are about 17 times larger, and
  their variance about 300 times larger, than A3 allows; 91 to 92 % of
  the (gene, replicate) values lie beyond $\pm2.33$, where 2 % are
  expected (@fig-fs-a3-shift). T4, the most conservative per gene,
  flags 6,147 (48 h), 6,220 (72 h) and 6,274 (96 h) of the 6,615 genes
  (`a3_shift_summary.csv`, @fig-fs-tail-flags). These flags measure the
  failure of A3, not a defect of individual genes.
- **The discrepancy is a gene-wise ratio.** For each gene and time,
  the mean over replicates of $\log_2\{(y_{gi}/a_i)/\sum_j\hat
  p_{ji}\hat{\tilde\mu}_{gj}\}$ (`platform_log_ratio()`) has an
  interquartile range of 2.0 to 2.2 across genes: half the genes are
  more than 2-fold away from the reference (`platform_log_ratio.csv`).
  The same genes are off in the same direction at every time: the
  Spearman correlation of the ratios is 0.97 (48 h–72 h), 0.95
  (72 h–96 h) and 0.94 (48 h–96 h) (@fig-fs-drift). 5,890 genes are
  flagged by T4 at two or three times with one sign; the 466 flagged
  with a sign change and the 226 flagged at one time only sit near a
  ratio of 0, where a small difference flips the sign or the flag.
- **The ratio follows transcript length.** The bulk is a full-length
  library and the reference a 3′ UMI library (protocols below), so a
  gene's bulk reads grow with its transcript length and its reference
  counts do not. The prediction is a slope of 1 of the log2 ratio on
  log2 length. The median-regression slope is 1.06 (48 h, 95 %
  gene-bootstrap interval 1.02 to 1.10), 1.18 (72 h, 1.13 to 1.22) and
  1.06 (96 h, 1.01 to 1.10); Spearman's correlation is 0.55 to 0.59, and
  a loess on length explains 31 to 34 % of the variance of the ratio
  (`platform_length.csv`, @fig-fs-length). Length is a large part of
  the platform effect, but two thirds of the gene-to-gene variation
  remain. The bootstrap treats genes as independent, so the intervals
  are too narrow if genes are correlated.
- **Dividing by a cross-fitted ratio.** With the free gene-wise ratio
  (estimated on the two other times), the interquartile range of the
  residual log2 ratio falls from 2.0–2.2 to 0.38–0.42, the share of
  genes more than 2-fold off from 51–54 % to 2–4 %, and the range rule
  flags 79, 309 and 82 genes instead of 3,179, 3,802 and 2,859
  (@fig-fs-bulk-fit, @fig-fs-tail-flags). The ratio learnt at 72 and
  96 h (primitive streak, mesoderm) transfers to the epiblast bulk at
  48 h, and conversely, so for most genes the effect belongs to the
  gene, not to a type. The length-only ratio removes less: residual
  interquartile range 1.5 to 1.6, range flags 2,007 to 2,940.
- **A residual remains.** With the gene-wise ratio the median
  $|z|$ is 2.0 to 2.2, and 44 to 48 % of the values lie beyond $\pm2.33$
  instead of 2 %; T4 still flags 4,628, 4,751 and 4,722 genes
  (@fig-fs-a3-shift). The residual log ratio (interquartile range about
  0.4 in log2 units, a 30 % spread) is far larger than both the
  negative-binomial sampling of the bulk and the uncertainty of the
  ratio itself (median standard error of $\log_2\hat b_g$ 0.06 to 0.07,
  `platform_ratio.csv`). Three sources are possible, none tested here:
  a ratio that depends on the type as well as the gene, which is not
  identified without paired measurements; biological differences
  between the gastruloids profiled in bulk and in single cell, which
  are different specimens; and errors of the plug-in composition. Our
  reading is that the tail statements need an extra between-platform
  overdispersion, fixed at 1 (none) here, before their flags can single
  out genes.
- **Two side effects.** The MAD rules flag more genes with the ratio
  (587 to 720 against 299 to 463), because one of their summaries is a
  bulk-to-reference ratio. The model-free quantile band flags 191 to
  203 genes with the ratio and 154 to 161 under A3, 2.3 to 3.1 % of the
  panel, near the 2 % it is fitted for.
  The residual log ratios are negatively correlated between times
  (Spearman −0.25 to −0.45): this is built in by cross-fitting, since
  each time's ratio is the average of the two others, and is not a
  drift.
- **Plug-in composition.** Under A3, epiblast takes all of the 48 h
  bulk and the primitive streak all of the 72 h bulk (shares of at least
  0.999), the types that dominate the reference (97 % and 93 % of the
  scored cells); at 96 h pre-somitic mesoderm takes 0.73 and caudal
  mesoderm 0.26. With the gene-wise ratio, the 48 h bulk becomes 0.91
  epiblast and 0.08 exiting naïve pluripotency, 72 h is unchanged
  (0.99 primitive streak), and the 96 h composition inverts: caudal
  mesoderm 0.72, pre-somitic mesoderm 0.25 (@fig-fs-plugin). The ratio
  used at 96 h was learnt at 48 and 72 h, where neither mesoderm type
  exists, so the genes that separate the two types carry ratios
  estimated from other cell states. No ground truth exists for these
  bulk samples: the inversion shows that the plug-in composition is not
  robust to the platform model, not which composition is right.
- **Cook's distance.** No gene is flagged in the weighted bulk fit at
  any time. This is a property of the deMixSC weights, not a finding:
  with $w_g=1/(\hat y_g^{2}+e_g^{2}+c)$, $\sqrt{w_g}\,|e_g|<1$, so the
  standardised residual is bounded (it stays within $\pm1.7$) and never
  reaches 3. Among cells, 21,686 to 27,679 (gene, cell) pairs are
  flagged per time, all in the small types, where a cell's leverage can
  exceed $3J/C$ (@fig-fs-cook).

**Gene-wise platform ratio: method.** The two libraries differ by
design. The bulk (GSE229386) is an Illumina Stranded mRNA Ligation
library of poly(A) RNA, aligned with STAR and counted with HTSeq on
GENCODE vM24 (mm10); the reference (GSE229513) is 10x Genomics Single
Cell 3′ v3, quantified with Salmon/Alevin on GENCODE M24 (GRCm38) (GEO
series records). Full-length single-cell protocols show the length bias
of bulk RNA-seq and UMI protocols do not
[TODO-cite: Phipson, Zappia & Oshlack 2017, Gene length and detection bias in single cell RNA sequencing protocols, F1000Research 6:595, doi:10.12688/f1000research.11290.1]{.highlight};
the bulk side is the transcript-length bias of RNA-seq counts
[TODO-cite: Oshlack & Wakefield 2009, Transcript length bias in RNA-seq data confounds systems biology, Biology Direct 4:14, doi:10.1186/1745-6150-4-14]{.highlight}.
The model, its identifiability conditions and the tail statements with
a plug-in ratio are in
[3.1, plug-in platform ratio](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-platform-ratio).
As applied here:

- **Length.** `gene_transcript_length()` averages the exonic length of
  the UCSC knownGene transcripts of each gene
  (`TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene` 3.10.0,
  `GenomicFeatures::transcriptLengths()`), matched by Ensembl id through
  `org.Mm.eg.db`, then by symbol: 6,564 genes by Ensembl id, 24 by
  symbol, 28 without a length. That annotation is based on GENCODE
  VM23, one release before the authors' vM24. Adapted from
  `annotate_genes_local()` of GastroDeconv2FateMap, which uses the
  genomic span instead (introns included).
- **Three variants, no filtering.** (i) A3, no ratio. (ii) A ratio from
  length: a robust loess of the per-gene median log ratio on log2
  length. (iii) A free gene-wise ratio: the deMixSC plug-in on
  $y_{gi}/\hat b_g$ alternates with $\log\hat b_g=$ median over the
  pooled replicates of the log ratio, until the largest change is below
  $10^{-3}$ (18 to 21 rounds; `estimate_platform_ratio()`). In (ii) and
  (iii) $\operatorname{median}_g\log\hat b_g=0$, since $a_i$ absorbs a
  common factor.
- **Cross-fitting.** The ratio used at one time is estimated on the six
  replicates of the two other times (`cross_fit_platform_ratio()`), so
  it cannot absorb the residual it is meant to test, and its transfer
  across compositions is what is tested.
- **Statistic.** `bulk_tail_filter(platform_ratio, platform_var)`
  divides the bulk by $\hat b_g$ before the plug-in fit, and adds the
  delta-method term $(\sum_j\hat p_{ji}\hat{\tilde\mu}_{gj})^{2}\operatorname{Var}\log\hat b_g$
  to the variance of $D_{gi}$ in $z$ and in T1; T1-log, T3, T4 and the
  module statements treat $\hat b_g$ as known. The RNA-Sieve range and
  MAD rules need no composition and run on $y_{gi}/\hat b_g$ as well.

What this changes: no gene is removed at this tier. A cross-fitted
gene-wise ratio removes most of the platform shift, so it belongs in
the model of tier (iv) rather than in a filter; the tail statements
become usable as a filter only once a between-platform overdispersion
is added for what the ratio leaves.

Orange: median regression; dashed: line of slope 1 through the medians, the prediction for a full-length bulk against 3′ UMI counts. The label gives the slope with its gene-bootstrap 95 % interval (1,000 resamples), Spearman's correlation and the share of variance explained by a loess. **Outputs.** At each time: the genes and modules flagged by
each statement; their overlap (pairwise Jaccard indices and an
UpSet-style table of membership patterns, `tail_flag_overlap()`); and
the order of the statements from the most to the least conservative,
read from the number of flags and the median thresholds, not assumed.
Across times: the drift class of each gene (`platform_drift.csv`), and
the settings of the run, including the smallest within-type correlation
for an edge of the dependency graph (`min_abs_cor = 0.1`,
`settings.csv`).

```{r}
#| label: fs-bulk-consistency-call
#| eval: false
# Not run. sc[[tm]]: raw counts (genes x cells) of the scored cells of
# slot tm, with labels cell_type[[tm]] and full library sizes lib[[tm]];
# bulk[[tm]]: the three standard-Wnt replicates at tm from GSE229386
# (raw counts, genes x samples), same gene identifiers; panel: genes
# selected by tier (ii) and the markers of tier (i).
source("R/02_00_utils.R")
source("R/02_01_stats_quality_control.R")
source("R/02_03_stats_tail_bounds.R")

# Step 1: p-free range check (RNA-Sieve range bound and MAD rule).
range_flags <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  x <- sc[[tm]][panel, , drop = FALSE]
  ct <- droplevels(factor(cell_type[[tm]]))
  norm <- sweep(as.matrix(x), 2L, sf[[tm]], "/")
  mu <- sapply(levels(ct), function(k) rowMeans(norm[, ct == k, drop = FALSE]))
  sd <- sapply(levels(ct), function(k) apply(norm[, ct == k, drop = FALSE], 1L, stats::sd))
  out <- bulk_consistency_filter(
    bulk = bulk[[tm]][panel, , drop = FALSE],
    mu = mu,
    sd = sd,
    n_cells = table(ct)[levels(ct)],
    z_range = 3,
    mad_k = 3
  )
  out$gene[!out$keep]
})

# Step 2: tail statements per gene and per module, and the quantile band.
dict <- utils::read.csv("data/dictionaries/mouse_gastruloid_signaling_markers.csv")
map <- map_marker_symbols(dict$gene_marker, universe = rownames(sc[["48h"]]))
dict$gene <- map$mouse_symbol[match(dict$gene_marker, map$gene_marker)]
modules <- lapply(
  split(dict$gene, dict$cell_type_excel),
  function(g) unique(stats::na.omit(g))
)
tail_res <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  bulk_tail_filter(
    bulk = bulk[[tm]][panel, , drop = FALSE],
    counts = sc[[tm]][panel, , drop = FALSE],
    cell_type = cell_type[[tm]],
    modules = modules,
    level = 0.01,
    c_reg = 2,
    max_degree = 10L,
    mean_degree = 3,
    min_abs_cor = 0.1
  )
})
names(tail_res) <- times
overlap <- lapply(tail_res, function(r) tail_flag_overlap(r$gene, band = r$quantile_band))

# Step 3: drift of the discrepancy across the three matched times.
drift <- platform_drift_summary(lapply(tail_res, function(r) r$gene), statement = "T4")

# Step 4: does the bulk / reference ratio follow transcript length?
# ensembl[panel]: Ensembl ids of the panel genes (bulk row names).
log_ratio <- platform_log_ratio(tail_res)
lengths <- gene_transcript_length(panel, ensembl[panel])
log2_length <- setNames(log2(lengths$mean_tx_length), lengths$gene)
length_test <- platform_length_test(log_ratio$log_ratio, log2_length, seed = 20261109L)

# Step 5: cross-fitted platform ratio (each time from the two others),
# then the same statements on bulk / b. No gene is removed.
mu_list <- lapply(tail_res, function(r) r$moments$mu)
ratio_gene <- cross_fit_platform_ratio(bulk, mu_list, method = "gene", n_iter = 30L)
ratio_length <- cross_fit_platform_ratio(
  bulk, mu_list, method = "length", log2_length = log2_length, n_iter = 30L
)
tail_gene <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  r <- ratio_gene[[tm]]
  bulk_tail_filter(
    bulk = bulk[[tm]][panel, , drop = FALSE],
    counts = sc[[tm]][panel, , drop = FALSE],
    cell_type = cell_type[[tm]],
    modules = modules,
    platform_ratio = setNames(exp(r$log_b), r$gene),
    platform_var = setNames(r$var_log_b, r$gene)
  )
})
```

{{< pagebreak >}}

## Tier (iv): down-weighting by the model {#sec-fs-weighting-pointer}

Tier (iv) is a remark, not a step of this chapter. Tiers (i) to (iii)
keep or drop a gene; tier (iv) keeps every gene of the exported panel
and lets the model weight it, so that genes with a large or poorly
estimated within-type covariance count less in the generalised least
squares of DeCovarT. That weighting happens only when DeCovarT itself
is fitted on the panel of @sec-fs-export, with the covariances
estimated in @sec-cov-scope, in the deconvolution of
@sec-deconv-models. No gene is selected and no code runs here. Why
weighting can replace a hard filter is in
[3.1, down-weighting](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-weighting).

## Panel export {#sec-fs-export}

The current export is the legacy one:
`scripts/01_03_export_equal_type_seurat.R` subsets the allow-list
Seurat object to the 500 genes of the type-equal ratio
([type-equal ratio](#sec-fs-ms-ratio)) at each time and writes
`data/intermediate/equal_type_top500_by_time.rds`, the input of every
script of @sec-cov-scope. Its `nCount_RNA` is recomputed on the 500
genes and is not a library size. That file stays the input until the
new rank has been run.

The new rank table will have one row per gene and time, with the
columns of @tbl-fs-new-rank-columns.

| Block | Columns | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Identifiers | `time_point`, `gene` | slot |
| Tier (i) gene rules | `fractional_share`, `in_sct_layer`, `shared_with_bulk` | `fractional_count_share()`, `gene_filter_rules()` |
| Presence gate | `min_detection`, `weakest_type`, `pass_presence` | `presence_gate()` |
| Fits and effect size | `overdispersion`, `deviance_m0`, `deviance_m1`, `deviance_r2` | `compare_type_effect_tests()` |
| Four tests | `<test>_stat`, `<test>_pval`, `<test>_padj`, `<test>_pass` for `lr`, `anova_vst`, `ql_f`, `welch_perm` | same |
| Gate and rank | `gate_test`, `adj_pval`, `pass_fdr`, `rank`, `selected` | `rank_genes_omnibus()` |
| Tier (i) markers | `in_marker_panel`, `in_union` | signalling dictionary |
| Tier (iii) outliers | largest cell Cook's distance, number of flagged cells, gene Cook flag per replicate | `cook_cells()`, `cook_genes()` |
| Tier (iii) bulk flags | range flag; one flag per statement (T1, T1-log, T3, T4, quantile band), any replicate, under A3 and with the cross-fitted gene-wise ratio; module flags; drift class across times; mean transcript length; $\log_2\hat b_g$ and its standard error | `bulk_consistency_filter()`, `bulk_tail_filter()`, `platform_drift_summary()`, `gene_transcript_length()`, `cross_fit_platform_ratio()` |

: Planned columns of the new rank table. Not written yet. {#tbl-fs-new-rank-columns}

## Perspectives {#sec-fs-perspectives}

### Cell-line sensitivity at 48 h {#sec-fs-cell-line}

The reference has one specimen per slot, so cross-sample consistency
([3.1, cross-sample](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-cross-sample))
cannot be tested. The closest available analogue is the two cell lines
at 48 h, the only slot that contains both. It is not part of the main
results. The script
`output/naive_marker_selection/cell_line_48h/01_03_sensitivity_48h_cell_line.R`
refits the legacy v2 model inside B-S and inside SBR and compares the
equal-cell top 500 and the per-type top 50. (It lives under `output/`
next to its results; `scripts/01_03_export_equal_type_seurat.R` is a
different script.)

- The two global lists share 308 of 500 genes (Jaccard 0.45).
- Epiblast shares 29, and exiting naïve pluripotency 30, of its top 50.
- Naïve pluripotency is scored in SBR only: B-S has fewer than 20 cells
  of that type.

Outputs: `overlap_48h_cell_line.csv`, `ranks_global_48h_by_line.csv`,
`ranks_per_cell_type_48h_by_line.csv`, `venn_48h_cell_line.pdf`.

### Comparison with classifier-based marker selection {#sec-fs-classifiers}

A second check of the panel uses classifiers of the cell type, each
inside stability selection [@meinshausenStabilitySelection2010], as in
[S6, sparse classifiers](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/S6-feature-screening-scenario.html#sec-sparse-classifiers):

- penalised multinomial logistic regression (`glmnet`, grouped lasso
  across types);
- sparse PLS discriminant analysis (`mixOmics::splsda()`);
- random forest (`ranger`, impurity importance).

[TODO-cite: glmnet (Friedman, Hastie & Tibshirani 2010); mixOmics (Rohart et al. 2017); ranger (Wright & Ziegler 2017)]{.highlight}

`classifier_markers()` (`R/02_05_classifiers.R`) subsamples half of
the cells of each type 100 times, keeps the top 50 genes of each fit,
and reports each gene's selection frequency; the stable set is the
genes selected in at least 60 % of the subsamples. The cells come from
one specimen, so the resampling unit is the cell and the frequencies
measure generalisation to new cells of this specimen
(@nte-pseudoreplication). The purpose is to check that the panel is
biologically meaningful, robust and able to discriminate the types, not
to replace it: the stable sets are compared with the omnibus panel
through their overlaps (`set_overlap()` in `R/02_00_utils.R`).

```{r}
#| label: fs-classifiers-call
#| eval: false
# Not run.
source("R/02_00_utils.R")
source("R/02_05_classifiers.R")
clf <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  g <- ranked[[tm]]$gene[ranked[[tm]]$pass_presence]
  classifier_markers(
    sc[[tm]][g, ],
    cell_type[[tm]],
    size_factors = sf[[tm]],
    n_subsample = 100L,
    frac = 0.5,
    n_top = 50L,
    threshold = 0.6,
    seed = 20261104L
  )
})
names(clf) <- times
clf_overlap <- lapply(times, function(tm) {
  stable <- split(clf[[tm]]$gene[clf[[tm]]$stable], clf[[tm]]$method[clf[[tm]]$stable])
  set_overlap(c(stable, omnibus = list(ranked[[tm]]$gene[ranked[[tm]]$selected])))
})
```

### Optional multivariate refinement {#sec-fs-nsga2 .appendix}

A univariate rank ignores redundancy between genes and the
covariances DeCovarT models. The optional stage searches subsets of
the panel with a multi-objective criterion on all types jointly
([3.1, covariance-driven (post hoc) selection](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-multivariate)).
It needs $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$, so it runs after
@sec-cov-scope, and it is drawn dashed in @fig-pipeline. Its panels
fall under the circularity warning of the vignette
([3.1, circularity](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#wrn-fs-circularity)):
a comparison with other methods also reports the panel of
@sec-fs-export, chosen without the model.

**Shortlist.** The multi-donor pipeline of the screening appendix
([S6, multi-donor pipeline](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/S6-feature-screening-scenario.html#sec-recommended))
feeds NSGA-II with a `DESeq2` pseudo-bulk shortlist. With one
specimen, as for the Suppinger reference, the `DESeq2` step does not
apply, and strategy B of that appendix (presence gate, omnibus gate,
effect-size rank; @sec-fs-presence and @sec-fs-omnibus) replaces the
shortlist.

**Types with few cells.** A joint test or objective on the panel
$\mathcal{G}$ uses the within-type covariance, which is
high-dimensional when $C_j$ is not much larger than $|\mathcal{G}|$
([3.1, multivariate tests](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-1-feature-selection.html#sec-fs-multivariate-tests)).
With the 500-gene panel of @sec-fs-export, seven of the eleven scored
type × time cells of @tbl-fs-cell-counts have $C_j<|\mathcal{G}|$, so
their sample covariance is singular:

- 48 h: exiting naïve pluripotency (265 cells), naïve pluripotency (36);
- 72 h: ectopic pluripotency (266), naïve pluripotency (66);
- 96 h: gut (140), ectopic pluripotency (116), somite differentiation
  front (29).

Caudal mesoderm at 96 h (1,061 cells) is about twice the panel size.
For these types the objectives below use the regularised
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ of @sec-cov-scope, never the
sample covariance.

Planned settings:

- **Optimiser.** NSGA-II through `mco::nsga2()` [@R-mco]. Genes are
  encoded as a mask in $[0,1]^{G}$, thresholded to a target panel size.
- **Objectives**, all minimised:
  1. the 2-norm condition number $\kappa_{2}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\mathcal{G}})$
     of the mean signature restricted to the panel;
  2. the mean pairwise `MixSim` overlap of the $J$ Gaussians
     $\mathcal{N}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j})$
     [@melnykovMixSimPackageSimulating2012; @R-MixSim];
  3. optionally, minus the smallest eigenvalue of the Fisher
     information for $\boldsymbol{p}$, as a sensitivity objective on a
     shortlist of non-dominated panels.
- **Output.** The whole Pareto front, not one panel. With one
  specimen, any panel chosen here is fitted on this atlas and has to
  be challenged on an external gastruloid cohort.

`scripts/04_02_feature_selection_genetic_algorithm.R` is a template:
it stops with an error until the fitness function is implemented on a
real panel.

```{r}
#| label: fs-nsga2-sketch
#| eval: false
# Not run. mu: G x J means; Sigma: list of J covariances (G x G), both
# on the linear scale, from the estimator selected in the covariance
# chapter.
fitness <- function(mask) {
  g <- which(mask > 0.5)
  kappa2 <- kappa(mu[g, , drop = FALSE], exact = TRUE)
  ov <- MixSim::overlap(
    Pi = rep(1 / J, J),
    Mu = t(mu[g, , drop = FALSE]),
    S = simplify2array(lapply(Sigma, \(A) A[g, g, drop = FALSE]))
  )
  c(kappa2, mean(ov$OmegaMap[upper.tri(ov$OmegaMap)]))
}
front <- mco::nsga2(fitness, idim = nrow(mu), odim = 2L,
  lower.bounds = rep(0, nrow(mu)), upper.bounds = rep(1, nrow(mu)))
```

## Legacy panel: SCTransform ratio {#sec-fs-legacy .appendix .unnumbered .unlisted}

The current 500-gene panel, and every covariance output of
@sec-cov-scope, come from the rank described here. It stays the source
of `data/intermediate/equal_type_top500_by_time.rds` until the rank of
tiers (ii) and (iii) has been run; it is kept as provenance of the
existing files.

### `SCTransform` v2 fit per time {#sec-fs-sct .unnumbered .unlisted}

`rank_genes_sctransform()` refits `Seurat::SCTransform()` separately at
48 h, 72 h and 96 h (`split_by = "time_point"`) on the allow-list
genes. Cells of every non-artefact type at that time are fitted
together. The fitted mean is an intercept plus a library-size offset,

$$
\log\mu_{gc}
=
\beta_{0g}
+
\log s_{c},
\qquad
x_{gc}\sim\mathrm{NB}(\mu_{gc},\psi_{g}),
$$ {#eq-fs-v2-offset}

with $s_{c}$ the full RNA library size of cell $c$ (column sum of the
unfiltered count matrix, stored as `log_umi` $=\log_{10}s_{c}$), not the
sum over the allow-list. The Pearson residual is
$r_{gc}=(x_{gc}-\hat\mu_{gc})/\sqrt{\hat\mu_{gc}+\hat\mu_{gc}^{2}/\hat\psi_{g}}$.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `vst.flavor` | `"v2"` (depth slope fixed at $\ln 10$ on $\log_{10}s_c$, i.e. an offset) |
| `method` | `"glmGamPoi"`; fitter recorded as `glmGamPoi_offset` |
| `vars.to.regress` | none |
| Cell type, cell line in the fit | no, no |
| `ncells` | all retained cells of the slot (10,891 at 48 h, 4,619 at 72 h, 4,935 at 96 h) |
| `residual.features` | all allow-list genes; `return.only.var.genes = FALSE` |
| `do.correct.umi`, `do.scale`, `do.center` | `FALSE`, `FALSE`, `TRUE` |
| `seed.use` | 1 |
| Residual clip | $\pm\sqrt{n/30}$: $\pm 19.05$ (48 h), $\pm 12.41$ (72 h), $\pm 12.83$ (96 h) |

: `SCTransform` settings as run (`model_card.csv`, `scripts/legacy/02_90_stats_rank_sctransform.R`). {#tbl-fs-sct-settings}

Cell type is left out of the fit on purpose. The count models of
@sec-fs-glm fit the type effect directly, without regularising the
overdispersion and without the clip.

### Between/within ratio rank {#sec-fs-ms-ratio .unnumbered .unlisted}

The residual matrix of one slot is split by type. With $C_j$ cells of
type $j$, $\bar r_{gj}$ the mean residual of gene $g$ in type $j$, and
$v_{gj}$ its within-type variance, the two decompositions are

$$
\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{between},g}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{J}C_{j}\bigl(\bar r_{gj}-\bar r_{g}\bigr)^{2},
\qquad
\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{within},g}
=
\sum_{j=1}^{J}\sum_{c\in j}\bigl(r_{gc}-\bar r_{gj}\bigr)^{2}
$$ {#eq-fs-ss}

(every cell has weight one), and

$$
\bar r_{g}^{\mathrm{eq}}
=
J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\bar r_{gj},
\qquad
\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{between},g}
=
J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}(\bar r_{gj}-\bar r_{g}^{\mathrm{eq}})^{2},
\qquad
\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{within},g}
=
J^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}v_{gj}
$$ {#eq-fs-equal-type}

(every type has weight $1/J$). The score is the ratio of the between
term to the within term.

Two global lists are built per slot (`anova_ss()`,
`anova_ms_equal_type()`, `rank_ratio()`):

1. **Global, equal cell weight.** Top `n_genes_global = 500` genes by
   $\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{between}}/\mathrm{SS}_{\mathrm{within}}$
   (`ranks_global.csv`). The largest type dominates.
2. **Global, equal type weight.** Top 500 by
   $\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{between}}/\mathrm{MS}_{\mathrm{within}}$
   (`ranks_global_equal_type.csv`). This list feeds the export of
   @sec-fs-export.

Each list is then united with the signalling markers of the types
scored in that slot (@sec-fs-markers). At 48 h the leading equal-cell
ratios land on naïve-pluripotency markers; at 96 h the top gene is the
endoderm marker *Sox17*. The residual clip changes only the far tail of
these ratios.
